description: We are a multidisciplinary team combining medical sciences and engineering to design health monitoring software for long-duration space missions. By integrating biological data analytics, software engineering, and system architecture, our platform delivers real-time, actionable insights to ensure astronaut safety, health, and operational readiness.
summary:
As humanity extends its reach beyond Earth-proximal, stable environments like the International Space Station into long-duration deep-space transit, missions face a critical barrier: complete operational isolation and severe communication latency. Real-time consultation with terrestrial medical infrastructure becomes impossible when signal delays stretch into minutes or hours, or when complete communication blackouts occur. Furthermore, the harsh realities of the space environment—including cosmic radiation, microgravity, and prolonged confinement—impose relentless physiological and psychological stressors on the human body.

V² is designed to bridge the gap between raw biological telemetry and proactive clinical action. By scaling seamlessly across both short-term orbital deployments and extended deep-space voyages, the platform provides adaptive oversight that responds to varying environmental demands. It equips crews with the continuous awareness needed to navigate complex physiological shifts, ensuring that astronauts are never left vulnerable to the hidden toll of long-term spaceflight.

Ultimately, V² redefines crew self-sufficiency in the cosmos. By transforming how biological and environmental data are interpreted and managed autonomously, the platform ensures that deep-space explorers remain physically resilient, mentally stable, and operationally independent—safeguarding human life no matter how far from Earth the journey takes them.
details:
𖤐 Project summary

Vitals of the Void is a next-generation aerospace telemetry and crew health management system built for long-duration deep-space missions. Because extended spaceflight cuts crews off from immediate terrestrial medical infrastructure, our platform bridges the gap between raw biological data and proactive clinical intervention. By integrating the TARS AI companion, and a robust symptom-triage architecture, the software instantly detects biological anomalies, runs predictive drift analyses, and generates clear, actionable medical guidance. Featuring seamless emergency escalation protocols and real-time clinical autonomy, Vitals of the Void ensures that astronauts are continuously safeguarded against the unpredictable physiological hazards of the deep void.

𖤐 Project description

During extended spaceflights, astronauts face severe environmental stressors—including cosmic radiation, social isolation, microgravity, and closed ecosystems—that trigger profound physiological risks like bone demineralization, immune dysfunction, and cardiovascular strain. To address this, Vitals in the Void features a dual-mode tracking architecture combining non-invasive continuous telemetry (suit/wristband sensors for real-time vitals) with invasive periodic laboratory analysis (serum, electrolyte, and biochemical assays).

The platform also incorporates dynamic threshold adjustments tailored to mission length and rate-of-change algorithms to track the velocity of physiological shifts and prevent false-positive alert fatigue. Mission-critical safety protocols feature a top-sidebar red emergency button and a hands-free voice activation trigger ("TARS code red") for rapid crisis management and direct telemetry transmission to NASA Earth command centres when a disease is suspected to cause a future disruption or illness.

𖤐 Key features

⬩➤ TARS AI Companion: A personal AI assistant powered by Gemini that switches between clinical medical guidance and crew peer support. To keep the astronaut both entertained but also informed about their current medical progress. (Uses Free API key; Subjected to limited uses)

⬩➤ Drift Vector Forecasting: Predictive forecasting models showing how environmental hazards cascade into physiological changes over 24–48 hours.

⬩➤ Supply Management (SUPPLIES): Tracks medical lockers, emergency kits, pharmaceuticals, and expiration dates aligned with NASA HRP guidelines and NASA-STD-3001. This feature keeps the food supplies and medical supplies in check during long distance space missions to keep the astronaut informed about the storage as well as recommend diet plans making efficient use of the limited sources.


⬩➤ AI Dermatology & Rash Triage: Since skin rashes are known to be some of the most common types of skin diseases which can occur in zero gravity in a accelerated manner, A Interactive questionnaires (RASH_Q and DX) for diagnosing microgravity skin conditions, contact dermatitis, and suit friction injuries has been added to counter this.

⬩➤ Earth Flight Surgeon Uplink: Automated anomaly warnings prompt astronauts to compile and send secure escalation packets for direct feedback from ground medical command. We have taken into account that getting real-time feedback from earth surgeons comes with a delay. We have made a feature that detects symptoms of a astronaut earlier on and determines weather these symptoms have a predictive drift that can cause a potential emergency. The astronaut will get a alert suggesting to speak to a earth surgeon earlier on to prevent any future emergencies and also saving time.

The expected trajectory will be shown and any countermeasure that can be taken during the wait to get a response from the earth space surgeon will be provided.

𖤐 How does Vitals in the void (V²) work?

Engineered for versatility across diverse operational environments—from stable platforms like the International Space Station to unforgiving long-duration deep-space missions—V² adapts seamlessly to safeguard astronaut health. Through continuous, close monitoring and adaptive clinical intelligence, the platform provides robust countermeasures designed to protect crew members from escalating health risks, actively mitigating NASA's five most critical physiological and psychological spaceflight concerns.

⬩➤ Dual-Mode Tracking Architecture: The system ingests data through two distinct pathways:

Non-Invasive Monitoring: Streams real-time vitals via smart wristbands and suit sensors, tracking over 50 physiological, biochemical, and environmental metrics (such as heart rate variability, continuous interstitial glucose, core body temperature, radiation dose rates, and upper-body fluid shifts).Invasive Periodic Laboratory Assays: Manages scheduled serum, electrolyte, and biochemical analyses to track deep-space physiological drift.

By harmonizing rigorous health oversight with proactive behavioural support, V² ensures that crew members remain both physically protected and mentally resilient. Beyond tracking vital telemetry, the platform integrates TARS—an adaptive AI companion designed to provide dynamic companionship, conversation, and clinical assistance. To combat the psychological toll of isolation and loneliness during both short-term operations (such as ISS deployments) and extended deep-space transit, the software features a dedicated suite of behavioural countermeasures. These include engaging mini-games, psychomotor vigilance testing (PVT), and private journaling tools designed to keep astronauts mentally stimulated, emotionally balanced, and at ease far from home. Along with this, there is also a wide range of appearance customisation options that can make the software personalised to the astronaut.

V² also has a emergency option that can work both manually (by clicking the button on the left) or hands-free through TARS. This creates a emergency alert that will alert the NASA earth base as well as other astronauts in the crew of any emergency situations during spaceflight.

𖤐 Tools and coding languages used

⬩➤ Tools used :

╰┈➤ motionsites.ai : used for UI of the software

╰┈➤ Claude : coding of the software

╰┈➤ AI studio : coding and UI of the software

╰┈➤ Gemini : for brain storming and general queries

╰┈➤ Clinical guidelines : NASA Human Research Program (HRP) guidelines and NASA-STD-3001 spaceflight standards.

⬩➤ Coding languages used :

╰┈➤ python : Used for the web server and API, the health model, warnings and alerts, Drift Vector forecasts, simulated crews, supplies, journal encryption, rash check, emergencies, saving and continuing missions, and TARS's AI connection

╰┈➤ JavaScript : Used for everything that runs in the browser: screens, charts, buttons and forms, TARS's chat, listening and speaking, the tours, wallpapers, the boot animation and the games

╰┈➤ Bash : Used for setting up and updating the Azure server

╰┈➤ HTML : Used for the page structure (sidebar, top bar, screens, pop-ups)

╰┈➤ CSS : Used for all the visual design (glass tiles, blur, grain, colours, layout, animations, mobile view)

╰┈➤ SVG : Used for icons, the body map and the charts

╰┈➤SQL : Used for storing and reading crew, measurements, supplies, journal entries and saved missions

╰┈➤ JSON : Used for medical reference data, the saved AI key, and API messages

╰┈➤ config files : Used for HTTPS and the web server, keeping the app running, and project settings

╰┈➤ markdown : Used for the project instructions

𖤐 Factors considered

⬩➤ Communication Latency: Designed entirely around the reality of deep-space communication blackouts where real-time support from Earth flight surgeons is impossible.

⬩➤ Microgravity & Space Environment Hazards: Accounted for severe spaceflight physiological stressors, including Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS), rapid bone mineral density (BMD) loss, fluid shifts, and cosmic radiation.

⬩➤ Usability & Alert Fatigue: Carefully calibrated thresholds and rate-of-change algorithms to prevent constant false alarms while ensuring immediate response capabilities for genuine crises.

⬩➤ Compliance & Safety Standards: Ensured all medical protocols, countermeasure checklists, and supply tracking frameworks directly align with NASA Human Research Program standards and NASA-STD-3001.

𖤐 V² standout points

⬩➤ Cinematic Sci-Fi Aesthetics: Blends rigorous biomedical utility with an immersive, full-viewport sci-fi design, making complex telemetry intuitive and engaging for astronauts under high-stress conditions.

⬩➤ Personality-Driven AI Companion: TARS goes beyond a standard chatbot by incorporating adjustable humour/honesty sliders and specialized voice synthesis, serving as both a clinical assistant and a comforting crewmate.

⬩➤ Space-Tailored Innovations: Introduces unique solutions specifically built for the realities of spaceflight—such as the interactive dermatology triage questionnaire (RASH_Q) for suit rashes and 24–48 hour predictive drift vector forecasting.

⬩➤ Games : various games added to keep the astronaut engaged during long space missions

⬩➤ Supply logging system : V² is designed to ensure that it meets the dietary requirements of the astronaut while effectively warning and making use of the supplies available on-board.
